newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan bans police,military from Hong Kong visits.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan bans police,military from Hong Kong visits.

text.p: Taipei said on Tuesday it was banning military and police visits to Hong Kong now that the territory is part of communist China, Taiwan's arch rival.

From July 1, soldiers and police cannot make sightseeing or other pleasure visits to Hong Kong due to security concerns, though exemptions can be made to visit ailing kin or attend funerals, a Defence Ministry spokesman said by telephone.
"It's a matter of national security," the spokesman said.
"Since Hong Kong has reverted to mainland sovereignty, we feel it's necessary to apply the same regulations governing mainland visits to Hong Kong," he said.
The tightened rules on visiting the former British colony makes them identical to restrictions long applied to visits to the communist-ruled mainland itself.
Exemptions to join international conferences or business activities would be granted on a case-by-case basis.
Taiwan has said the island's extensive civilian contacts and exchanges with Beijing-ruled Hong Kong would remain unchanged.

Beijing, which has seen Taiwan as a renegade province since a 1949 civil war split, maintains that the return of Hong Kong, and Portuguese-run Macau in 1999, will leave Taiwan as the only territory still awaiting "reunification with the motherland".
Taipei officially espouses reunification with the mainland but only when all of China is under a free, democratic system.
